title: What made a four-frame shopkeeper animation look wrong in my Android game
author: ZookeepergameOdd9524
selftext:
I’m working on Rune Survivors in Flutter and Dart. I used image generation to turn a portrait of the skeleton shopkeeper into four idle poses, then used Codex to wire up playback. The first version looked like the whole shop was breathing. The shelves and counter moved a few pixels between frames, even though the hand was supposed to be the only thing moving.



The fix was to draw the first frame as a fixed background, then clip the other frames to the outline of the raised hand and potion. I tried keeping the skull animated too, but its edges shifted against the stationary hood, so I kept the head fixed. For the spell tab I used a separate pose with an open book and painted the rune on top in Flutter, timed to the four hand poses. That kept the line drawing independent of the generated frames.



If you’ve animated AI-generated sprites this way, how do you handle seams when a moving prop crosses the mask?



The game is free with ads on Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.runesurvivors.game](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.runesurvivors.game)
